name: cargo-nextest
why: Test runner used by CI (`cargo nextest run --workspace`). Runs each test in its own process, which matters here because agent-profile tests spawn the binary and the fake-agent fixture and set per-process environment. Does NOT run doctests — pair with `cargo test --doc`.
gates: `just check`; CI Test job on ubuntu, macos, windows

name: just
why: Task runner and the single entry point for the local gate. `just check` = fmt-check + clippy + typos + shellcheck + line-citations + test + probe-tests + tools-doc-check + doc-check. Configured by the root justfile.
install: cargo binstall -y just  (any platform; Ubuntu also has `sudo snap install --classic just`)
gates: everything — local gate, pre-push hook and CI all route through the recipes it defines

name: lefthook
why: Git hooks. pre-push runs `just fmt-check`, `just clippy` and `just typos` in parallel; there is no pre-commit hook, so commits stay fast. Routing through just keeps the hook and CI from drifting apart. Configured by lefthook.yml; needs `lefthook install` once per clone.
install: NOT ON crates.io — `cargo binstall lefthook` fails with "lefthook is not found", and the crates.io API returns "crate `lefthook` does not exist" (verified 2026-10-07). Linux: download the `.deb`/`.rpm`/`.apk` from github.com/evilmartians/lefthook/releases (e.g. `curl -sSL -o /tmp/lefthook.deb .../lefthook_<ver>_amd64.deb && sudo dpkg -i /tmp/lefthook.deb`) · macOS: `brew install lefthook` · Windows: `scoop install lefthook`, or the release binary. Then `lefthook install` once per clone.
config: `lefthook.yml` (pre-push: fmt-check, clippy, typos in parallel; no pre-commit)

name: cargo-deny
why: Advisory, licence, ban and source auditing across the dependency graph. Configured by deny.toml, which pins the allow-listed licences, bans openssl-sys (V3 spec §36: no hidden network activity) and lists the per-platform target triples.
config: `deny.toml` (licence allow-list, `openssl-sys` ban per V3 §36, 7 target triples)

name: typos
why: Spell-checks source and prose; runs as its own CI job and in `just check`. Configured by _typos.toml, which excludes the delivered V3 spec.

name: bacon
why: Background check/clippy/test watcher during development (`just watch`). Configured by bacon.toml; default job is check-all.

name: cargo-mutants
why: Mutation testing (`just mutants`) for the invariant-heavy library: profile-name validation, resolution precedence, config atomicity. .gitignore already excludes mutants.out*.

name: actionlint
why: Lints the GitHub Actions workflows. Runs the shell in each `run:` step through shellcheck when shellcheck is on PATH; without it that check is silently skipped (visible only with `actionlint -verbose`).
install: Linux: `go install github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@latest`, or download the release binary to ~/.local/bin · Windows: `winget install rhysd.actionlint`

name: shellcheck
why: Lints every `.sh` under sandbox/ and scripts/ as its own gate recipe, and lets actionlint check the shell inside workflow `run:` steps — actionlint disables that rule when shellcheck is not on PATH. Version matters: `ubuntu-latest` carries an older build than a current local install, and the two disagree on SC2317 versus SC2329, so `sandbox/run.sh` carries both codes.
install: Linux: `sudo apt install shellcheck` · Windows: `winget install koalaman.shellcheck`
gates: `just check`, CI Shellcheck; also lets actionlint lint the shell inside workflow `run:` steps

name: disposable agent sandbox
why: Coding agents are NEVER installed on the host (CONTRIBUTING.md "Measuring agent behaviour"): adapter evidence is refreshed only inside a disposable box. The box differs by platform, which is why this entry is satisfied by ANY of them — Sandboxie-Plus on Windows, Podman or Bubblewrap on Linux, Tart or OrbStack on macOS. It used to name Sandboxie-Plus alone with a Windows-only path, so it reported missing on every Linux and macOS clone; the paths below are checked with ANY semantics, so whichever box this platform uses satisfies it.
install: Linux: `sudo apt install podman` (or `bubblewrap`) · Windows: `winget install Sandboxie.Plus` · macOS: `brew install tart` (see CONTRIBUTING.md)

name: podman
why: The container engine `sandbox/run.sh` runs the probe harness in, and the one CI uses (`AGENT_PROFILE_SANDBOX_ENGINE: podman` in both sandbox.yml jobs). Docker is an accepted fallback and run.sh selects it automatically when podman is absent, but the two are NOT equivalent here: run.sh passes `--userns=keep-id:uid=1000,gid=1000` ONLY under podman, so anything about uid mapping across the /out bind mount is unreproducible under Docker. That matters for the two-user privilege boundary, where a second uid writing the mount is the specific hazard. ON WINDOWS, `sandbox/run.sh` CANNOT COMPLETE FROM GIT BASH AT ALL — measured 2026-09-23 with podman 5.8.3 and a warm cache: without `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV` the image builds and `eng run` dies on `--volume "$root:/src:ro"` because MSYS rewrites the container-side `/src`, and with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` the build dies first on a mangled context path. Both settings fail, in different places, so on Windows use the Actions Sandbox workflow instead. On Linux it runs natively and local probing is the fast path.
install: Linux: `sudo apt install podman` · Windows: `winget install RedHat.Podman` then `podman machine init && podman machine start` (and see the Git Bash limitation above)
gates: on demand; `.github/workflows/sandbox.yml` runs the same on a GitHub runner with **podman** (probes by hand; `test` on PRs that change the harness)

name: rustup / rustc / cargo
why: Installs and manages the Rust toolchain pinned by rust-toolchain.toml (stable, with rustfmt + clippy); every other tool here builds or runs through it.
install: Linux/macOS: `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh` · Windows: `winget install Rustlang.Rustup`

name: rustfmt
why: Formats Rust source. Ships as a rustup component; enforced in the local gate, the pre-push hook and CI.

name: clippy
why: Lints Rust source with warnings promoted to errors. Ships as a rustup component; enforced in the local gate, the pre-push hook and CI.

name: cargo-binstall
why: Installs the other cargo-based tools here (cargo-nextest, just, lefthook, cargo-deny, typos-cli, bacon, cargo-mutants) from prebuilt binaries instead of compiling each from source.
